name: TX-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+13 partisan lean in a Houston-area district
Polymarket prices Democratic win at just 4%
Steinmann has raised over $2 million with outside support; Jones has raised under $25,000
model.rationale: The district's R+13 lean, the Republican's overwhelming fundraising advantage, and prediction markets pricing the Democrat at 4% all point to a safe Republican hold despite the open seat. No polling or expert ratings suggest any reason to move toward the Democrat.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic spending or an unexpected Republican primary fallout could narrow the margin, though a genuine upset remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview: Republicans are strongly favored to hold this Houston-area seat, which Morgan Luttrell is leaving open. The district carries a R+13 partisan lean, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 4% chance of winning. Republican Jessica Hart Steinmann has raised about $2.1 million and benefits from roughly $1.7 million in outside support, while Democrat Laura Jones has raised under $25,000 with no outside spending on either side. The open-seat dynamic removes the incumbent from the ballot but does little to change the underlying partisan balance. The forecast expects a comfortable Republican win in the mid-teens, with modest uncertainty given the absence of public polling in the race.
